custom.commandCenter.contractHint: This page supports selected-device jobs and capped filtered-fleet jobs with preview token, per-device progress, timeout refresh, retry, cancel, and support bundle evidence. Background workers and offline callback reconciliation are still separate backend work.
custom.commandCenter.progressDesc: Move through target scope, preflight, submit, and support evidence. The current step is highlighted so handoffs are easy to read.
custom.commandCenter.progressScopeReadyD: Target devices or filters are ready for job preflight.
custom.commandCenter.progressScopeTodoDe: Select devices from Fleet or use a saved filter as the command target.
custom.commandCenter.progressPreviewRead: Preflight is ready. Review eligible devices, skipped reasons, and safety caps.
custom.commandCenter.progressPreviewTodo: Run preflight to see which devices will be targeted and which will be skipped.
custom.commandCenter.progressPreviewWait: Waiting for a target scope before preflight can run.
custom.commandCenter.progressSubmitReady: The job has been submitted; track per-device results and audit evidence.
custom.commandCenter.progressSubmitTodoD: Submit the job after preflight so device-level outcomes are recorded.
custom.commandCenter.progressSubmitWaiti: Waiting for preflight before the job can be submitted.
custom.commandCenter.progressSupportRead: The support bundle is ready to copy to operators, customer success, or engineering.
custom.commandCenter.progressSupportTodo: Generate a support bundle with failed devices, retry advice, and Ready Check links.
custom.commandCenter.progressSupportWait: Support bundle and closeout evidence are available after the job is submitted.
custom.commandCenter.recentRunningJobDes: Job {jobId} was still scheduled or running when you last viewed it. Open it to keep tracking progress.
custom.commandCenter.savedFilterPickerDe: Switch the command target without returning to Fleet. Changing filters clears the old preview; if a command identifier is already filled, preview runs again.
custom.commandCenter.savedFilterEmpty: This saved filter has no usable command target.
custom.commandCenter.savedFilterLocalOnl: Only browser-local saved filters are available in this workbench. Refresh when the backend saved-filter list is reachable.
custom.commandCenter.savedFilterLocalFal: Backend saved filters could not be loaded, so Command Center is using browser-local saved filters.
custom.commandCenter.savedFilterRouteMis: The saved filter in the URL is no longer available. The current filter payload is still visible, but the saved identity should be cleared before handoff.
custom.commandCenter.savedFilterRenameFa: Could not rename the saved filter. Check the name and try again.
custom.commandCenter.savedFilterDeleteFa: Could not delete the saved filter. Refresh and try again.
custom.commandCenter.deleteSavedFilterCo: Delete this saved filter from Command Center?
custom.commandCenter.previewExplainDesc: This section shows what the operator is targeting, what the backend recalculated, and why submit is locked or unlocked.
custom.commandCenter.immediateDesc: Use this path when the first selected device is online and the operator needs a quick request-response confirmation.
custom.commandCenter.immediateCheckOnlin: Confirm the device is online before sending.
custom.commandCenter.immediateCheckMessa: Keep the message ID for troubleshooting.
custom.commandCenter.immediateCheckRespo: Read the device response, error, or timeout evidence after sending.
custom.commandCenter.jobsDesc: Preview selected devices and submit commands only to eligible rows. Use the scope warnings to avoid mistaking this for a persisted fleet Job.
custom.commandCenter.quickStarterDesc: Choose a common operation to fill the command name, JSON payload, and timeout, then review the exact device scope before submitting.
custom.commandCenter.templateNeedsScope: Choose devices or a saved filter first; templates only prepare the command after the target scope is known.
custom.commandCenter.saveCommandTemplate: Command template saved locally. Preview again before submitting.
Enter a command identifier before saving a template.
custom.commandCenter.savedCommandTemplat: Templates store command content only. The target scope still comes from this page.
No payload saved for this template.
custom.commandCenter.applyCommandTemplat: Template filled the command draft. Preview before submitting.
custom.commandCenter.importCommandTempla: Paste exported command-template JSON from support or another operator. Import stores command content only; the target scope still comes from this page.
No valid command templates were found in that JSON.
Imported {count} command templates. Preview before submitting.
custom.commandCenter.scopeSafetyMeta: Templates and history only fill command content. Preview recalculates this scope before submit.
custom.commandCenter.scopeSafetyNoScopeD: No device target is selected yet. Choose devices or a saved filter before previewing.
custom.commandCenter.scopeSafetySelected: This job targets {count} selected devices from the current page handoff.
custom.commandCenter.scopeSafetySavedFil: This job uses saved filter {name}. Backend matched {total}; current-page subset is {currentPage}; submit cap is {max}.
custom.commandCenter.scopeSafetyFiltered: This job uses {filters} active filters. Backend matched {total}; current-page subset is {currentPage}; submit cap is {max}.
custom.commandCenter.templateRebootDesc: Use for online devices that need a controlled reboot and clear job evidence.
custom.commandCenter.templateSyncDesc: Ask devices to pull or apply their latest platform configuration.
custom.commandCenter.templateDiagnoseDes: Request status, log, and telemetry evidence before escalation.
custom.commandCenter.jobRequirementScope: Current scope: selected devices passed from Fleet. Current-page and matching counts are context only.
custom.commandCenter.jobRequirementEligi: Preflight: online state, firmware version, credentials, and device capability.
custom.commandCenter.jobRequirementProgr: Result: this request returns per-device submitted/blocked/failed status, message ID, log state, and reason.
custom.commandCenter.jobRequirementRetry: Controls: refresh the persisted job, cancel pending rows, or retry failed rows after reviewing the reason.
custom.commandCenter.jobRequirementAudit: Evidence: keep job ID, message ID, operator context, log state, timestamps, and failure reason for troubleshooting.
custom.commandCenter.previewBeforeOta: Preview the filtered command scope before opening OTA so the OTA flow receives the same reviewed device scope.
custom.commandCenter.preflightDeferredDe: Command drafting, preview, and submit controls stay ready first. Scroll here or load this panel when you need the static scope contract and filter summary.
custom.commandCenter.noSelection: Select devices from the Fleet page before opening immediate commands or Jobs.
custom.commandCenter.noFilterScope: Open Command Center from a Fleet filter or selected devices before previewing a filtered command job.
custom.commandCenter.selectionReady: Selection is ready for command routing or OTA job preflight.
custom.commandCenter.filterScopeReady: Filtered scope is ready for a capped command job. Preview must return the full matched set before submit is enabled.
custom.commandCenter.filterScopeDraftWar: Filtered-fleet command jobs expand the current filter on the backend and are capped for safety. If the match count is too high, narrow the filter or raise the approved max before submitting.
custom.commandCenter.filterScopeSummary: {filters} filter fields, {total} matching devices, {currentPage} current-page subset devices.
custom.commandCenter.filterScopeBackendR: This backend does not yet accept the filtered-fleet job contract.
custom.commandCenter.commandValue: Command value or JSON params, optional
custom.commandCenter.commandValueInvalid: Command value must be valid JSON.
custom.commandCenter.payloadAssistantEmp: This command will send only the identifier. Add JSON when the device expects parameters.
custom.commandCenter.payloadAssistantVal: The payload is valid JSON with {fields} top-level field(s). Preview will use this exact content.
custom.commandCenter.payloadAssistantInv: This looks like JSON but cannot be parsed. Fix it before preview so operators do not send a broken payload.
custom.commandCenter.payloadAssistantPla: This is not valid JSON. If the device expects text, wrap it as a JSON string such as "restart now".
custom.commandCenter.scheduleImmediateHi: Leave blank to dispatch immediately. Choose a future time within one year in your current time zone.
custom.commandCenter.scheduleInvalid: Choose a valid scheduled start time.
custom.commandCenter.scheduleMustBeFutur: Scheduled start must be in the future. Clear it to dispatch immediately.
custom.commandCenter.scheduleTooFar: Scheduled start cannot be more than one year from now.
custom.commandCenter.maxDevicesHint: Filter matches {matched} devices. Safety cap: {max}; preview subset: {subset}. Submit unlocks only when preview covers every matched device within the cap.
custom.commandCenter.previewBeforeSubmit: Command content or device scope changed. Preview again before submitting.
custom.commandCenter.submitBlockedPrevie: Preview the command job before submitting.
custom.commandCenter.submitBlockedChange: Command content, timeout, safety cap, or device scope changed. Preview again before submitting.
custom.commandCenter.submitBlockedNoElig: Preview found no eligible devices to submit.
custom.commandCenter.submitBlockedSubset: Preview covers only a subset: showing {shown} of {matched} matched devices. Narrow the filter or raise the approved safety cap ({max}) before submitting.
custom.commandCenter.routeDecisionSummar: Route advice: {immediate} devices can use immediate command, {jobs} should use offline/batch Jobs, {blocked} still need attention; {telemetry} have current telemetry evidence.
custom.commandCenter.previewPlanDesc: Use this before submit to see which devices are ready, which need a Job, and which blockers need attention.
custom.commandCenter.previewTokenSummary: Preview locked the current device state and command content with check {token}. If device state or command content changes before submit, the backend will require a new preview.
custom.commandCenter.previewDisplayLimit: Showing the first {shown} of {total} preview rows to keep this page responsive. {hidden} rows are hidden here, but submit still uses the full eligible preview and token.
custom.commandCenter.filteredPreviewFull: This preview covers the full submitted scope: {shown}/{matched} rows are represented, with {eligible} eligible and {blocked} blocked in the visible evidence. Route advice can be treated as full preview evidence.
custom.commandCenter.filteredPreviewSubs: This is a subset preview, not full fleet evidence: {shown}/{matched} matched devices were checked here. The subset shows {eligible} eligible, {blocked} blocked, {immediate} immediate, {jobs} Jobs, {pathBlocked} blocked-path devices, and {telemetry} rows with telemetry. Submit stays locked until the preview covers the full approved scope.
custom.commandCenter.submitCapabilitySum: Command job boundary: cancel {cancel}, retry failed devices {retry}. A successful submit means the platform accepted dispatch, not that the device finished execution.
custom.commandCenter.nextActionRetry: Retry this device after reviewing the failure reason.
custom.commandCenter.nextActionRetryAfte: Retry after {time}; review the failure reason before sending again.
custom.commandCenter.nextActionRetryLimi: Retry limit reached. Inspect device state, command logs, and support evidence before creating a fresh attempt.
custom.commandCenter.nextActionRefreshLo: Refresh the job or copy the support bundle; platform log evidence is missing.
custom.commandCenter.nextActionFixBlocke: Fix the blocker shown in the reason before sending again.
custom.commandCenter.nextActionCompleted: No action needed; keep the evidence if this was a customer-facing operation.
custom.commandCenter.nextActionDeviceAck: Device returned success. Keep response evidence and verify state if needed.
Device returned failure. Review response evidence before retrying.
custom.commandCenter.nextActionTrackMess: Track the message ID and refresh until the device result is terminal.
custom.commandCenter.nextActionSupportBu: Copy the support bundle if the result is unclear.
custom.commandCenter.submitEvidenceSumma: Failure closure: {retryable} devices can be retried, {missingLogs} are missing platform log evidence. Review reason, then refresh, cancel, or retry.
custom.commandCenter.jobProgressSummary: Progress: {submitted} submitted, {failed} failed, blocked, or canceled, {total} total.
Keep auto-refresh on and wait for pending devices.
Watch closely; prepare to review evidence if pending rows do not finish.
Refresh the job, review timed-out rows, and use retry or support evidence before creating another attempt.
Review failed, blocked, missing-log, or device-response rows before retrying or handing off.
Keep the canceled job link for audit and create a new preview if the operation still needs to run.
Job is ready to close; keep the link and support evidence with the customer record.
custom.commandCenter.deviceProgressDesc: Track each device from preview readiness through dispatch, device acknowledgement, and platform evidence.
custom.commandCenter.deviceProgressPrevi: Preview blocked this device before dispatch.
custom.commandCenter.deviceProgressEvide: Platform command-log evidence is still missing.
custom.commandCenter.actionConsequenceDe: Confirm which devices each action will affect before changing this job.
custom.commandCenter.actionConsequenceCa: Cancel will stop {pending} pending or in-flight rows while the job is {status}; late device ACKs may still arrive as audit evidence.
Cancel is unavailable while the job is {status}. Keep refreshing or copy evidence instead.
custom.commandCenter.actionConsequenceRe: Retry can requeue {ready} ready failed devices. {waiting} are waiting for the retry window and {exhausted} reached the retry limit.
Retry is unavailable until failed devices become retry-ready.
custom.commandCenter.actionConsequenceWa: {count} devices are cooling down; refresh after the retry window.
custom.commandCenter.actionConsequenceEx: {count} devices reached the retry limit and need support review before another attempt.
custom.commandCenter.actionConsequenceDe: {count} devices returned failure from the device; review response evidence before retrying.
custom.commandCenter.actionConsequenceLo: {count} rows are missing platform log evidence; refresh before closing or escalating.
custom.commandCenter.outcomeDesc: Group platform dispatch evidence by retry, log refresh, blocker fixes, continued tracking, or confirmed device completion.
custom.commandCenter.outcomeRetryDesc: Review the reason, then retry only these devices.
custom.commandCenter.outcomeDeviceFailed: Review device-side error evidence before retrying.
custom.commandCenter.outcomeMissingLogsD: Refresh the job or copy the support bundle before closing the operation.
custom.commandCenter.outcomeBlockedDesc: Fix readiness, online state, command path, or permission blockers before sending again.
custom.commandCenter.outcomeInProgressDe: Track message IDs and refresh until each row reaches a terminal state.
custom.commandCenter.outcomeCompletedDes: The device reported a terminal success state; keep the evidence for customer handoff.
custom.commandCenter.troubleshootingDesc: Use this checklist to decide whether to refresh, retry, cancel, or copy evidence for support.
custom.commandCenter.troubleshootingRetr: {count} failed devices are retryable. Retry only after checking the reason column.
{count} devices are waiting for the retry window.
custom.commandCenter.troubleshootingCanc: {count} rows are not terminal yet. Cancel them if the operation should stop.
custom.commandCenter.troubleshootingLogs: {count} eligible devices are missing platform log evidence. Refresh before closing the job.
custom.commandCenter.troubleshootingBloc: {count} devices were blocked before dispatch. Review readiness, online state, and command path.
custom.commandCenter.troubleshootingSupp: Copy the support bundle and keep the job link before handing off or closing the operation.
custom.commandCenter.operatorDecisionEvi: Evidence: {retryable} retryable, {pending} pending, {missingLogs} missing logs, {blocked} blocked, {deviceFailed} device-response failures.
custom.commandCenter.operatorDecisionDev: {count} devices reported failure from the device. Check response evidence before retrying.
custom.commandCenter.operatorDecisionRet: Retry only the failed retryable devices
{count} devices are retryable. Confirm the reason, then retry this failed subset.
{count} devices are cooling down before retry.
{count} devices reached the retry limit and need support review.
custom.commandCenter.operatorDecisionRef: {count} rows are still pending or in flight. Refresh before changing the job.
custom.commandCenter.operatorDecisionLog: {count} eligible rows are missing platform log evidence. Refresh before closing or escalating.
custom.commandCenter.operatorDecisionBlo: Fix blocked devices before sending again
{count} devices were blocked before dispatch. Fix readiness, online state, permission, or command-path blockers.
custom.commandCenter.operatorDecisionDon: Job is ready for handoff or closure
No urgent dispatch action remains. Keep the job link or support bundle with the customer record.
custom.commandCenter.operatorDecisionSup: Preview the support bundle and keep the job link before handing off this operation.
custom.commandCenter.autoRefreshDeferred: Auto-refresh paused while rows or support evidence load
custom.commandCenter.downloadSupportBund: Could not download the support bundle. Preview or copy it instead.
custom.commandCenter.resultRowsDisplayLi: Showing {shown} loaded result rows for the current filter/search. {hidden} more matching rows are still available; load more for row-level triage or use the support bundle for the full handoff.
custom.commandCenter.rowsSearchPlacehold: Device, message ID, failure reason, or response
custom.commandCenter.rowsScopeSummary: Showing {shown} of {total} matching rows. Filter: {filter}. Search: {search}.
custom.commandCenter.rowsNoMatchDesc: Filter {filter} and search {search} returned no device rows. Clear the search, show all rows, or generate a support bundle for the job scope.
custom.commandCenter.jobAttentionSummary: {count} need action: {retryable} retryable, {deviceFailed} device failures, {missingLogs} missing logs
custom.commandCenter.supportBundlePrevie: Review the support bundle before copying it to another operator or support channel.
custom.commandCenter.openDeviceDiagnosis: No device ID is available for diagnosis.
The job will enter the dispatch queue after its scheduled start.
custom.commandCenter.jobHistoryDesc: Refresh previous persisted jobs, open details, reuse safe command drafts, then retry, cancel, or copy a support link from the same workbench.
custom.commandCenter.jobHistoryDeferredT: Load command history only when needed
custom.commandCenter.jobHistoryDeferredD: Keep command drafting and preview responsive first. Scroll here or click the load action when you need persisted job search, attention filters, and support links.
custom.commandCenter.jobHistoryAttention: Counts below come from the whole filtered history result, not only the rows currently loaded.
custom.commandCenter.reuseJobDraftSucces: Command draft filled from history. Preview again before submitting.
custom.commandCenter.saveJobAsTemplateSu: Historical job saved as a local command template.
custom.commandCenter.reusedDraftDesc: Copied command {identify} from job {jobId}. Target scope, preview token, and submit gate still come from the current page, so preview before sending.
custom.commandCenter.routeDraftDesc: Loaded command {identify} from {source}. This only fills the draft; preview and submit gates still protect execution.
custom.commandCenter.jobHistoryEmpty: No persisted command jobs yet. Preview and submit a command job first.
custom.commandCenter.jobHistoryEmptyDesc: Choose devices from Fleet or a saved filter, enter a command identifier, preview the target scope, then submit the first tracked Job.
custom.commandCenter.copyFailedDeviceIds: No retryable failed devices to copy.
custom.auth.authFailedPleaseLogin: Authentication failed or insufficient permissions. Please login again.
custom.commandCenter.guideDesc: Move through selection, input, preview, and submit. The page shows what is ready and what needs attention.
custom.commandCenter.guideSelectDesc: Choose devices from Fleet, then return to Command Center to continue.
custom.commandCenter.guideIdentifyDesc: Use the command identifier from the device model, with optional JSON value or params.
custom.commandCenter.guidePreviewDesc: Check permissions, device capability, and payload before any device receives the command.
custom.commandCenter.guideSubmitDesc: Submit only eligible devices and keep message ID, log state, and failure reason for follow-up.
custom.devicePage.firstDeviceOnboardingT: You are setting up the first device
custom.devicePage.firstDeviceOnboardingD: Keep going with manual add, then use the connection details and Ready Check to confirm the device is online and publishing telemetry.
custom.device_details.accessGuideHiddenT: {count} test code blocks are deferred so the first screen does less code highlighting.

custom.device_details.twinConfirmationAc: Comparable desired/reported values are aligned. Review the evidence boundary, then continue with commands, OTA, or batch Jobs.
Ask the device to report again, refresh this view, and continue only after reported values appear.
Compare delta rows before claiming device execution or starting OTA/command work.
Review expired desired state and update it before sending more operations.
Create desired state or wait for reported evidence before using this view as execution proof.

Boundary: review the evidence source before treating this as execution proof.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.title: AetherLink operations workspace for {userName}
custom.dashboardWorkbench.description: Start with device access, then confirm telemetry, twin state, commands, OTA, and alarm closure evidence.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.capabilityDevi: Create a device, copy MQTT/HTTP parameters, publish the first test telemetry event, and download handoff proof.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.capabilityRead: Confirm connection, latest telemetry, partial evidence, and next actions before field handoff.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.capabilityTwin: Compare desired and reported state, keep delta boundaries visible, and avoid false execution claims.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.capabilityComm: Preview target scope, submit bulk commands, track device rows, and export support bundles.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.capabilityOtaD: Use preflight, staged rollout evidence, failed-device representatives, and Ready Check handoff links.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.capabilityAlar: Acknowledge, reset, export closure evidence, and keep platform boundaries clear.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.readinessAcces: Access: keep MQTT/HTTP credentials local and prove one real telemetry publish.

custom.dashboardWorkbench.readinessSuppo: Support: every handoff bundle must say what it proves and what it does not prove.
custom.dashboardWorkspace.title: Open visualizations and dashboards
custom.dashboardWorkspace.description: Use this entry to organize ThingsVis projects, open dashboard lists, and return to the operations workspace when you need device, alert, OTA, or command context.
custom.dashboardWorkspace.projectsDesc: Create or open visualization projects for device telemetry, alarms, and fleet operations.
custom.dashboardWorkspace.dashboardsDesc: Manage existing dashboards and continue editing screens tied to a selected project.
custom.dashboardWorkspace.workbenchDesc: Return to first-device, Ready Check, Command Jobs, OTA, and alarm closure flows.
custom.dashboardWorkspace.handoffDesc: Open Projects when creating visualizations, Dashboards for existing screens, or Workbench when you need device health, OTA, alarms, and command context.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.activityFirstD: Create a device, publish one test telemetry event, and download the handoff proof.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.activityComman: Check the selected fleet scope before submitting bulk commands.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.activityReadyC: Confirm connection, latest telemetry, and evidence boundaries for support.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.activityOtaAla: Inspect rollout preflight and close alerts with downloadable evidence.
custom.dashboardWorkbench.activityVisual: Open ThingsVis and bind dashboards to live telemetry, alarms, and fleet status.
custom.home.setup.createSuperAdmin.title: Create the system administrator first
custom.home.setup.createSuperAdmin.descr: The platform has not finished first-time initialization yet. Create the system administrator before creating a tenant and onboarding the first device.
custom.home.setup.createTenantAdmin.desc: The system administrator is ready, but there is still no tenant. Create a tenant administrator or tenant before coming back to onboard the first device.
custom.home.setup.loginAsTenantAdmin.tit: Switch to a tenant administrator account
custom.home.setup.loginAsTenantAdmin.des: Initialization is complete, but the current account has no tenant context. Sign in with a tenant administrator account before creating the first device.
custom.home.setup.ready.title: Tenant setup is complete
custom.home.setup.ready.description: This account already has tenant context and can start onboarding the first device now.
custom.home.resume.afterCreate: Last time you created {deviceName}. You can continue with {lastTitle}.
custom.home.resume.continue: Last time you stopped at {lastTitle}. You can continue with {lastAction}.
custom.home.firstRun.setupRequired: {title}, then come back to create the first device.
custom.home.firstRun.deviceCreated: Created the first {protocol} device. Refreshing access parameters now.
custom.home.firstRun.deviceCreateFailed: Failed to create the first device. Try again later or switch to manual creation.
custom.home.sysAdminSetup.missingDashboa: Configure the super-admin home dashboard first
custom.home.sysAdminSetup.unavailableDes: ThingsVis is not responding right now, so the home dashboard cannot be loaded yet. Core features like devices, alarms, and system settings are still available while you wait.
custom.home.sysAdminSetup.nativeTenantCo: Select a tenant for the Native home dashboard

custom.home.sysAdminSetup.missingDashboa: No native home dashboard is configured yet. Open Native dashboards, create one, add widgets in the local editor, and set it as the home dashboard to show it here.
custom.home.dashboardSection.title: Existing home dashboard
custom.home.dashboardSection.description: The first-device onboarding loop stays at the top of the home page, and the original ThingsVis dashboard remains below it.
custom.home.dashboardSection.deferredDes: To keep the onboarding guide and device status available sooner, the iframe and live resources load only after this section scrolls into range.
custom.home.compatNotice.title: Compatible home configuration detected
custom.home.compatNotice.description: This tenant still keeps a compatible home layout record. To keep first-device onboarding, online status, latest telemetry, and the first chart more reliable, the retired classic cards are no longer rendered here.
custom.home.compatNotice.statusAvailable: First-device onboarding, online status, latest telemetry, and the first chart entry remain available.
custom.home.compatNotice.statusManageInT: If the home presentation still needs maintenance, manage it from the ThingsVis project.
custom.home.browserTest.httpEndpointUnav: The HTTP access endpoint is not a reachable URL yet. Open Ready Check to finish the setup first.

custom.home.browserTest.simulationNotRea: Simulation parameters have not finished loading yet.
custom.home.browserTest.mqttRequestSent: The MQTT simulated telemetry was sent. Refreshing the latest data now.

custom.management.user.backToHomeForDevi: Back to home to connect a device

header to call the plugin access API. Once you reveal a key, the requests below switch to the real key. Replace
with the service identifier of your protocol plugin.
custom.management.api.noApiKeyHint: There is no API key yet. Add a key first, then copy a runnable request. The API isolates data by the tenant that owns the key.
custom.devicePage.fleetSelectedActionsDe: Run immediate actions that need confirmation on the {count} selected device(s).
custom.devicePage.fleetScopeActionsDesc: Use the {count} device(s) on the current page as the scope. Useful for pre-release checks and handover.
custom.devicePage.fleetEvidenceActionsDe: Review alarms, audit records, and the selected-device summary for the current scope. Gather evidence before running bulk actions.
custom.deviceOperations.workbenchIntro: The device operations workbench links access, telemetry, twin, commands, alarms, and diagnostics into one next-step path. Online status last updated:
custom.deviceOperations.readyDesc: Confirm the device profile, connection parameters, latest telemetry, and recommended next fixes.
custom.deviceOperations.telemetryDesc: Review current telemetry, field status, and history trends to confirm the device keeps reporting.
custom.deviceOperations.twinDesc: Compare desired/reported/delta to see whether the cloud intent was acknowledged by the device.
custom.deviceOperations.commandDesc: Send a single-device command and review the receipt. When the device is offline, check access status first.
custom.deviceOperations.alarmDesc: Review rules, alarm state, and handling entry points so a red dot always comes with a next step.
custom.deviceOperations.diagnosisDesc: Aggregate connection, command, and telemetry diagnostics to locate the cause of access failures.
custom.device_details.debugModeTooltip: When enabled, the system records this device’s communication messages for troubleshooting.
custom.device_details.diagnosticSummaryC: Diagnostic summary copied. Sensitive fields are masked.
custom.device_details.nextActionUplink: Check the device reporting topic / HTTP path, the field format, and whether the latest telemetry was stored.
custom.device_details.nextActionDownlink: Check whether the downlink command was sent, whether the device is online, and whether the device returned an execution receipt.
custom.device_details.nextActionAuth: Check the authentication method, username, and credential status. Do not paste raw credentials into a support ticket.
custom.device_details.nextActionTopic: Check the topic mapping, the device-side subscribe/publish paths, and the thing-model identifiers.
custom.device_details.nextActionDisconne: Check the device network, the heartbeat/keep-alive configuration, and why the broker closed the connection.
custom.device_details.nextActionPayload: Check whether the payload JSON and field types match the thing-model definition.
custom.device_details.nextActionDefault: Using this timestamp, refresh Ready Check, the latest telemetry, and the device-side logs.
custom.device_details.nextStepErrorRefre: Refresh the diagnostic data and confirm that your session and the device detail API are still reachable.
custom.device_details.nextStepErrorReady: Open Ready Check or the onboarding guide, then resend a test telemetry message while comparing the device-side logs.
custom.device_details.nextStepEnableDebu: There is no explainable diagnostic evidence yet. You can enable debug mode briefly, then let the device reconnect or report one test message.
custom.device_details.nextStepDisableDeb: Do not leave debug mode enabled for long. Turn it off once you have the evidence.
custom.device_details.nextStepDebugNoLog: Debug mode is enabled but no logs have appeared yet. Let the device reconnect, publish telemetry, or run a command.
custom.device_details.nextStepCheckEndpo: If it is still empty, check whether the device connects to the MQTT/HTTP address of this environment.
custom.device_details.nextStepReviewLate: Review the next-step suggestion on the latest failure or log entry.
custom.device_details.nextStepCopySummar: Copy the diagnostic summary and send it to support. Do not paste raw credentials separately.
custom.device_details.summarySensitiveNo: Sensitive fields: password/token/secret/key/cookie and similar fields are masked. Do not paste raw credentials separately.
custom.luaEditor.loading: Loading the device data processing script editor...
custom.login.setup.createSuperAdminTitle: First launch: create the system administrator
custom.login.setup.createSuperAdminDesc: After the administrator is initialized, create a tenant and your first device.
custom.login.setup.createTenantAdminTitl: Next: sign in, then create a tenant admin
custom.login.setup.createTenantAdminDesc: A system administrator already exists, but there is no usable tenant yet. Sign in, open user management, and create a tenant admin first.
custom.login.setup.welcomeBackDesc: After signing in you can continue closing the loop on your first device onboarding.
custom.device_details.diagnosisFailureNe: Check the device uplink topic/HTTP path, field format, and whether the latest telemetry was stored.
Check whether the downlink command was sent, the device is online, and the device returned an execution receipt.
custom.device_details.diagnosisLogNextAu: Check the authentication method, username, and credential status; do not paste raw credentials into tickets.
custom.device_details.diagnosisLogNextTo: Check the topic mapping, device subscribe/publish paths, and thing-model identifier.
custom.device_details.diagnosisLogNextDi: Check the device network, heartbeat/keep-alive settings, and the broker disconnect reason.
custom.device_details.diagnosisLogNextPa: Check whether the payload JSON and field types match the thing-model definition.
custom.device_details.diagnosisLogNextDe: Refresh Ready Check, the latest telemetry, and device-side logs against the timestamp.
custom.device_details.diagnosisStepsErro: Refresh the diagnostics and confirm the current session and device-detail API are still reachable.
Open Ready Check or the access guide, and resend a test telemetry against the device-side log.
custom.device_details.diagnosisStepsNoDe: There is no interpretable diagnostic evidence yet. Briefly enable debug mode, then let the device reconnect or report a test payload.
Do not keep debug mode on for long; turn it off once you have the evidence.
custom.device_details.diagnosisStepsNoLo: Debug mode is on but no logs yet. Let the device reconnect, publish telemetry, or run a command.
If it is still empty, check whether the device is connected to the MQTT/HTTP endpoint of this environment.
custom.device_details.diagnosisStepsDefa: Review the next-step advice for the latest failure/log entries.
Copy the diagnostic summary to support; do not paste raw credentials.
custom.device_details.diagnosisCopySucce: Diagnostic summary copied; sensitive fields are masked.
custom.device_details.diagnosisSummarySe: Sensitive fields: password/token/secret/key/cookie and similar are masked; do not paste raw credentials.

custom.home.firstDevice.overview.title: First device verification
custom.home.firstDevice.overview.laneCon: Copy the access parameters or the test command first
The device finished its first onboarding round, so you can reuse these parameters for similar devices.
custom.home.firstDevice.overview.laneOpe: Copy the support summary if you are stuck

After downloading the success proof, hand it over with verification/startup-.../manifest.json for deployment acceptance, then run deploy/first-device-closeout.* to produce the final closeout manifest.
custom.home.firstDevice.identity.prepari: Loading deployment health, the first device, connection parameters, and the latest telemetry. You will land on the create or test step once it is ready.
custom.home.firstDevice.identity.loadWor: The home page shows the dashboard and the guide first to keep the initial load light. First-device details load only when you need access parameters, latest telemetry, or diagnostics.
custom.home.firstDevice.identity.createF: Pick an access protocol, then create the default product, things model, and first device in one click. After that copy the parameters, or let the browser publish one message to confirm the path.
custom.home.firstDevice.identity.protoco: Recommended: the built-in broker, publish commands, and simulated reporting path provide the most complete flow.
Best for environments where the HTTP access service is already configured; after creation, use the HTTP test code or a browser fetch test.
custom.home.firstDevice.identity.sequenc: Check API / DB / Redis / MQTT first
custom.home.firstDevice.identity.createF: Create the first device in one click
custom.home.firstDevice.identity.healthB: Check deployment health first. Confirm API, database, Redis, and the MQTT broker are healthy before creating the first device.
custom.home.firstDevice.identity.created: Created: {deviceName} ({protocol}). Click refresh if it does not show up right away.
custom.home.firstDevice.identity.confirm: Confirm device identity and online status
custom.home.firstDevice.connection.title: Connection parameters
custom.home.firstDevice.connection.openR: Open Ready Check to see it
custom.home.firstDevice.connection.helpe: Real devices connect with the current protocol. If you only want to validate the platform, use the browser test on the right.
custom.home.firstDevice.connection.tryIt: Click "Send test data from the browser" on the right, and the home page keeps confirming online status, latest telemetry, and the first chart.
custom.home.firstDevice.proof.latestTele: Latest telemetry and the first chart
custom.home.firstDevice.proof.chartGener: The first chart was generated automatically
custom.home.firstDevice.proof.chartWillG: The first chart will be generated automatically
custom.home.firstDevice.proof.chartPendi: After a browser test or a real device report, the home page builds the first chart from the latest telemetry automatically.
custom.home.firstDevice.proof.readyToDel: The device is ready to hand over

Download the success proof. It contains the device, connection parameters, browser test, online status, latest telemetry, and first-chart evidence. Hand it to the maintainer when archiving, and run deploy/first-device-closeout.* to produce the closeout manifest.
custom.home.firstDevice.proof.blockedFal: Keep following the loop strip above until every proof item turns green.
custom.home.firstDevice.proof.firstTelem: Still missing: send the first telemetry message. Copy the command to the device, or run the browser simulation. The first chart appears here once the home page receives data.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.title: Deployment health
custom.home.firstDevice.health.readyDesc: The frontend proxy, API, database, Redis, and MQTT are ready.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.pendingDe: Some dependencies are still not ready. Fix the red items before onboarding a device.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.checkFail: The health check did not pass
Select Check to confirm the frontend proxy, API, database, Redis, and MQTT broker.
The frontend proxy, API, database, Redis, and MQTT broker are all ready.
Fix the first red component, then run the check again.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.missingCh: {label} did not return a health check result
custom.home.firstDevice.health.defaultNe: Use the error to check the service, address, port, and credentials, then run the health check again.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.apiUnavai: The API health endpoint is unreachable
custom.home.firstDevice.health.checks.fr: The browser can reach the backend health endpoint through the frontend same-origin path.
Check the frontend Nginx or proxy configuration and confirm that browser requests to /api/v1 are forwarded to the backend.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.checks.ap: The backend health endpoint responded, so the API entry point is reachable.
Check that the backend service is running, its port is exposed, and the frontend API address points to this backend.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.checks.da: Business data, tenants, devices, and telemetry metadata depend on the database.
Start the database service, then verify the backend database address, account, password, and network.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.checks.re: Caching, sessions, and asynchronous state depend on Redis.
Start Redis, then verify the backend Redis address, password, and network.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.checks.st: Device online status is checked separately when it uses a dedicated Redis instance.
Check the device-status Redis configuration and confirm that a separately deployed instance is reachable from the backend.
custom.home.firstDevice.health.checks.mq: Device MQTT access and simulated reports depend on the broker connection.
Check that the MQTT broker is running, its port is exposed, and the backend MQTT adapter is connected to it.
custom.home.firstDevice.deferred.connect: The main navigation and the current step stay interactive first. The parameter card and the online tester load when you scroll here or jump to this section.
custom.home.firstDevice.deferred.proofHe: The success proof section is deferred
custom.home.firstDevice.deferred.proofDe: Finish the current onboarding step first. The first-chart proof and the handover download card load when you scroll here or use the button.
custom.home.firstDevice.deferred.support: The home page keeps the main onboarding flow interactive first. The support summary preview loads when you scroll here or use the button.
custom.home.firstDevice.tester.title: Web MQTT/HTTP online tester
custom.home.firstDevice.tester.desc: Copy the test command for a real device, or let the browser publish one telemetry message. On success the home page confirms online status, latest telemetry, and the first chart automatically.
custom.home.firstDevice.guide.desc: Get the first device working before moving on to automation and customer dashboards. The home page stays focused on this one loop instead of mixing later configuration into the first step.
custom.home.firstDevice.guide.readyAlert: The device is ready: {name} is online and has recent telemetry.
custom.home.firstDevice.guide.foundAlert: Found {name}. Online status and telemetry reporting still need to be confirmed.
custom.home.firstDevice.guide.emptyAlert: No device is available yet. Create a product, a things model, and the first device, then come back here to verify onboarding.
custom.home.firstDevice.guide.followupDe: Automation and dashboards stay in the second phase so they do not interrupt the first-device loop.
custom.home.firstDevice.support.title: Support summary
custom.home.firstDevice.support.desc: Send this to the maintainer when you are stuck. It includes device identity, access endpoint, latest telemetry, browser test, and failing deployment health items.
custom.home.firstDevice.support.sizeHint: Summary ready: {size}. The full content renders only inside the preview dialog.
custom.home.firstDevice.support.sizePend: Generated when you preview or copy
custom.home.firstDevice.strip.desc: One single path from the deployment check to the success proof. You do not need to learn device management, OTA, automation, or visualization first.
custom.home.firstDevice.wizard.title: First-run wizard
custom.home.firstDevice.wizard.desc: Follow these 5 steps: initialize the account and tenant, confirm deployment health, then create the device, send telemetry, and see the first chart.
custom.home.firstDevice.test.title: Get the parameters and send the first test
custom.home.firstDevice.test.desc: This is the first-device onboarding console: confirm the parameters, copy the command or test code, then send one test telemetry message straight from the browser.
custom.home.firstDevice.workspace.label: Current workspace
custom.home.firstDevice.canvas.title: Onboarding loop canvas
custom.home.firstDevice.canvas.desc: Follow the arrows from deployment to the first chart to get one device working. The orange node is what to handle now. Click a node to jump to the matching section below.
custom.home.firstDevice.workbench.minima: Clear things-model fields, the device online, telemetry with values, traceable alarms, and a shareable dashboard. Get one device working, then replicate it in bulk.
